key_insight: DVD deterministically adapts pre-trained video diffusion models into single-pass depth regressors by repurposing diffusion timesteps as structural anchors and using generative priors to resolve geometric ambiguity without stochastic hallucinations or scale drift.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off in video depth estimation where generative models produce stochastic geometry and scale drift while discriminative models require massive labeled data to disambiguate semantics.
method: Deterministic conversion of pre-trained video diffusion models into a single-pass depth regression pipeline (no iterative sampling).
Repurpose the diffusion timestep as a structural anchor to encode coarse-to-fine geometry and stabilize scale across frames.
Leverage generative priors from the pre-trained diffusion model to resolve semantic ambiguities and enforce temporal consistency without stochastic hallucinations.
impact: Delivers accurate, temporally stable depth from video without large labeled datasets, lowering the barrier for practical applications (robotics, AR/VR, 3D reconstruction) and reducing common generative failure modes like hallucination and scale drift.
visual_elements: Architecture flowchart: input video → adapted diffusion backbone → timestep-as-anchor module → single-pass depth output.
Qualitative panel: side-by-side frames showing RGB input, ground-truth depth, DVD output, and outputs from a generative and a discriminative baseline.
Metric charts: error vs. frame/time showing reduced scale drift and improved temporal consistency; accuracy vs. amount of labeled data to show label-efficiency.
Concept diagram: visualization of diffusion timestep acting as a coarse-to-fine structural anchor across frames.
paper_title: DVD: Deterministic Video Depth Estimation with Generative Priors
paper_authors: Hongfei Zhang, Harold Haodong Chen, Chenfei Liao, Jing He, Zixin Zhang
